title: Behavioral Drift Reef — Acceptance Matrix for Batch/Cache Cost Adjustments
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: provide a conservative, statistically grounded acceptance matrix and CI harness that validates behavioral fidelity when automated batch/cache recommendations are applied. This ticket builds an eval layer that pairs cost savings signals with semantic-quality checks and a human-audit escalation path. The output is an automated decision: allow config apply (auto), block and queue for human review, or trigger immediate rollback if regression exceeds thresholds.

Scope:
- Design and implement a stratified evaluation matrix that runs against representative traffic slices (short chat, long chat, instruction, embedding-heavy).
- Build a lightweight golden prompt corpus and stratified anchor sets per customer workload archetype.
- Define quantitative acceptance thresholds (embedding similarity, slot-F1, policy-safety checks, perplexity delta) and accompanying statistical tests.
- Integrate with canary runner to run pre-apply and post-apply checks and with rollout controller to orchestrate automatic rollback.
- Provide dashboards, alerts, and a human-audit UI with triage guidance.

Non-goals: end-to-end human-review tooling UX (we provide a simple form and links to the audit doc; UX team will iterate separately).
decisions: Use cosine similarity on embeddings (SBERT family) as primary semantic delta metric for open-ended output; fallback to turn-level token alignments for structured tasks.
Require both a statistical significance test (two-sided bootstrap of delta) and an absolute threshold to approve applies — prevents approval due to large sample variance.
Run golden-prompt smoke checks (deterministic anchors) as quick gate before full stratified eval to catch severe regressions fast.
Default policy: if cost saving >= 10% with semantic delta < threshold -> auto-apply; if delta borderline or customer_impact high -> staged canary with human review.
Keep human-in-loop for any drift affecting PII redaction or safety-related labels (always forward to security team).
rollout_plan: 1) Pre-apply quick smoke using 200 golden prompts (5s budget). 2) If pass, schedule a stratified evaluation run (n=1k samples across archetypes) during low-traffic window. 3) If stratified checks pass, start a 2-hour canary with 5% traffic and continuous monitoring. 4) If canary metrics hold, ramp to 25% for 6 hours then to 100% by policy. 5) If any step fails acceptance_criteria, run automated rollback and create incident with attached evaluation artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Semantic similarity (mean cosine) vs baseline on stratified set >= 0.94 OR delta <= 0.02 absolute.
- Structured-task slot-F1 drop <= 1.5 percentage points.
- Per-token perplexity increase <= 3%.
- Safety label regression (false-negatives) must be 0.
- Statistical test: two-sided bootstrap with 10k resamples, p-value < 0.05 required to conclude non-regression; both p-value AND absolute delta rule must be satisfied to allow apply.
- Minimum sample size per archetype: 200.
- Canary rollback trigger: any metric breach sustained for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows or single severe regression (>5ppt slot-F1 drop).
implementation_notes: Eval harness runs in a dedicated ephemeral k8s job with node selector for GPU-acceleration for embedding compute.
Docker image: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime/eval-harness:2025-03-07; include deterministic seeds and model pinning to avoid flakiness.
CI integration: job triggered by config-change PR or recommendation push; pre-apply runs are required for auto-apply eligibility.
Atomic apply uses feature-flagged rollout and config versioning; rollback leverages previous runtime snapshot (config_id) and invalidates cache if needed.
Monitoring: create short-window alerting on delta metrics in console; integrate with on-call runbook: runbook link in links[].
